title: Dependency Scorer and Visibility Stream for Quarterly Roadmaps
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Roadmap planning sessions repeatedly surface hidden cross-team blockers (design handoffs, infra quotas, security signoffs) that surface late and derail quarter-level rollouts. Existing trackers are a mix of spreadsheets, Slack threads, and ad-hoc Linear links with inconsistent severity and no single source of truth for prioritization across teams.

This ticket proposes building a Dependency Scorer and Visibility Stream: a lightweight scoring service plus visible feed (Console + Slack + Linear automation) to make all roadmap-level dependencies measurable, searchable, and actionable by PMs, Eng leads, Design, Security, and Infra. The goal is to reduce late-stage surprises, speed up mitigation, and feed measurable signals into quarterly planning and OKR tracking.
background:
We run quarterly roadmaps with cross-functional initiatives (Serving runtime, Dedicated, Private). During Q1 2026 planning, three initiatives were delayed by an average of 3 weeks due to unclear dependency ownership and late security reviews. Current artifacts are duplicated across teams (Confluence, Google Sheets) and lack prioritized, normalized severity. Engineering spends >4 hours/week re-triaging dependencies during rollouts.

We need a minimal, ops-friendly system that: (1) surfaces dependencies early, (2) scores them for prioritization and risk, (3) sends targeted actions to owners, and (4) plugs into existing dashboards and Linear workflows.
goals:
1) Create a standardized dependency model (type, owner, ETA, impact, blockers).
2) Implement a scoring algorithm to rank dependencies by risk and lead time.
3) Build a Visibility Stream that populates Console and posts summarized cards to a dedicated #roadmap-deps Slack channel.
4) Automate creation of follow-up Linear issues for top-tier risks and ensure each quarterly roadmap has a dependency heat-list before the final sign-off.
5) Track dependency completion rate and average lead time as OKR sub-metrics.
approach:
Phase 1 (MVP):
- Schema: define minimal fields (summary, type [design/infra/security/ops], owner, requested_by, requested_date, due_date, impact_level, blocking_work, mitigation_plan link).
- Scorer: rule-based weightings (impact_level x owner_response_slack_time x days_until_due) to surface high-risk items.
- Visibility: Console widget + Slack daily digest + weekly Linear automation that creates or updates a 'dependency' label on related issues.

Phase 2 (Iterate):
- Add telemetry signals (pipeline quotas, infra capacity forecasts, security queue times).
- ML-assisted clustering to dedupe similar dependencies across initiatives.
- Bi-directional sync with Design trackers and Security triage board.
scoring_model:
Initial heuristic:
- Impact: P0(5), P1(3), P2(1)
- Owner latency: average days to respond in past 90d mapped to multiplier (>=5d=1.5, 2-4d=1.2, <2d=1.0)
- Lead time pressure: days_until_due <14 => multiplier 1.4, <7 => 1.8
Score = base_impact * owner_latency_multiplier * lead_time_multiplier.
Top-20% scores flagged as 'High risk' and create Linear follow-ups automatically. Scorer is configurable via a small admin UI in Console.
notifications_and_stream:
- Console: Dependency Stream tab that can be filtered by initiative, owner, and risk.
- Slack: daily digest of new/high-risk items and direct pings to owners for critical blockers.
- Linear: automation that creates/updates linked dependency issues and adds 'dependency:critical' label when score crosses threshold.
- Email: weekly rollup to execs with trend lines for dependency inflow/outflow.
All notifications include suggested mitigations and links to relevant PRs, design specs, or infra dashboards.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console Dependency Stream displays seeded dependencies for three pilot initiatives with correct fields.
2) Scoring engine computes risk and flags top 20% as high-risk; results are visible in Console and Slack digest.
3) Automation creates/updates Linear issues for high-risk items and sets owner field.
4) Pilot teams (Runtime, Dedicated, Private) confirm that visibility reduced time-to-resolution for flagged items in pilot month by >=25%.
5) Documentation (owner guide + triage matrix) published and linked from Console.
milestones:
- 2026-03-15: Schema and scoring spec finalized (design/eng/security sign-off).
- 2026-03-31: MVP scorer + Console stream internal demo.
- 2026-04-14: Slack digest + Linear automation live for pilot.
- 2026-04-28: Pilot retrospective and metric baseline collection.
- 2026-05-01: Roll into Q2 roadmap sign-off process and expand to all initiatives.
stakeholders: PM: Lina Chen (roadmap owner), Engineering leads: Rohit Banerjee (serving runtime), Maya Patel (infra), Design lead: Oliver Grant, Security: Priya Singh, Analytics: Diego Alvarez (telemetry), DX: Hannah Lee (Console UI).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Owners ignore Slack pings -> Mitigation: fallback to Linear assignment + escalation path to Eng/PM leads.
Risk: Score produces noise and false positives -> Mitigation: initial conservative threshold, weekly tuning, and ability for owners to downgrade/update items.
Risk: Adding process overhead slows teams -> Mitigation: keep fields minimal, auto-suggest values from linked PRs/Issues, and run pilot with small set of initiatives first.
Risk: Security-sensitive metadata exposed -> Mitigation: stream respects role-based access in Console; secure links for sensitive docs.
metrics_and_targets:
- Dependency discovery lead time (days) — target: reduce by 30% at quarter end.
- High-risk dependency resolution time — target: <=14 days for 75% of flagged items.
- % of roadmap initiatives with zero high-risk dependencies at sign-off — target: 60%.
- Owner response SLA — target: initial acknowledgement within 48 hours for 90% of items.
rollout_plan: Pilot with three initiatives (serving runtime, dedicated capacity, private deployment) for 4 weeks. Iterate based on retrospective and metrics. After pilot, enable for all roadmap initiatives and add to quarterly sign-off checklist. Communicate via All Hands, Docs, and a short training video for PMs and Eng leads.
final_comment: This initiative is intended to be low-friction and highly actionable. The MVP focuses on surfacing the riskiest dependencies early; longer-term work will reduce duplication and automate more of the mitigation workflow. Expect to iterate scoring weights after two pilot cycles.
